meta.title: Verified Dataset — Subject Property SP-01 decision support
meta.subject: SP-01 — single-tenant Jack in the Box quick-service restaurant, NNN lease, central Los Angeles submarket, lease expiry window 2030–2035
meta.privacy: No address, parcel number, owner identity, tenant-unit identity, rent, or lease terms are recorded anywhere in this dataset. All parcel-specific values that would be required for a formal appraisal are deliberately absent and are listed as UNVERIFIED in the Assumptions section.

status_values.verified: Read directly from an official-primary source (see sources.json tier).
status_values.verified-secondary: Official statement read through a reproduction; caveat recorded on the source.
status_values.unverified: Could not be confirmed from an official source. Value is null and the row appears on the Flagged for Review page.

sections.title: Macro & Capital Markets
sections.why: Cap rates for single-tenant net-lease retail are priced off the long end of the Treasury curve plus a risk spread. This section fixes the discount rate the projection engine uses.

rows.note: Held at the October 2026 FOMC meeting on a 10–2 vote.

sections.title: Tenant Credit — Jack in the Box Inc.
sections.why: In a net-lease structure the landlord is, for the lease term, an unsecured creditor of the tenant. Tenant credit quality is therefore a direct determinant of lease-renewal probability and of the cap rate a buyer will accept.

sections.title: Tax, Transfer Cost & Regulatory Load
sections.why: These are the frictions that convert a headline sale price into net proceeds, and the recurring costs that determine what a buyer can pay.

rows.note: Plus incremental rates for locally voter-approved bonded indebtedness.

rows.metric: Proposition 13 annual increase cap on base year value
rows.note: Or the change in California CPI, whichever is lower.

rows.value: Change in ownership or completion of new construction
rows.note: A sale resets the base year to market value. This is the mechanism described in the tax-lock section.
Assessed value must be the lower of current market value or the adjusted base year value.
RTC §11911(a): $0.55 for each $500 or fractional part, on consideration or value exceeding $100. Effective rate $1.10 per $1,000.

rows.metric: City of Los Angeles base real property transfer tax
rows.note: Computed at $2.25 per $500 or part thereof.

rows.metric: Combined county and city transfer tax (below ULA threshold)
rows.note: Derived: 0.11% county plus 0.45% city. The two source rates are verified; the sum is arithmetic.
Applies to the whole consideration, not the marginal amount.
Indexed annually to BLS Chained CPI. It was $5.0M at enactment — it will be higher again by 2030.

rows.metric: Effective total transfer tax at or above the upper threshold
rows.note: 0.45% base plus 5.5% ULA. The city's own FAQ states the 5.95% figure.

rows.value: Limited to 501(c)(3), government, and constitutionally exempt transferees
rows.note: A private owner has no exemption. This is a pure cost of exit.

rows.value: Available for real property held for investment or business use
rows.note: Gain is recognised only to the extent of boot. Losses cannot be recognised. US real property is not like-kind to foreign real property.
Indexed to CPI-W, capped at 3.5% per year, and cannot be reduced.
Applies to limited-service chains of 60+ establishments nationwide, including franchisees. Directly binds the tenant's P&L.

rows.metric: Fast Food Council authority to raise the sector wage
rows.note: A standing body can raise the floor again. This is an unhedgeable operating-cost risk for the tenant and therefore a renewal risk for the landlord.

rows.metric: Owner's actual property tax basis and base year value
rows.note: Paramount to any hold-versus-sell decision and entirely unavailable without the parcel record. Do not model an assumed basis as fact; the model treats it as a stated scenario parameter.

rows.metric: Owner's federal and California marginal capital gains rates
rows.note: Depends on the owner's personal return. The model exposes this as a user-set scenario parameter and reports results across a range.

rows.metric: Remaining depreciable basis and accumulated depreciation
rows.note: Drives unrecaptured §1250 recapture on sale. Unavailable without the owner's return.

rows.metric: Effective total transfer tax just above the ULA lower threshold
rows.note: Computed on $6,500,000: county $7,150 + city $29,250 + ULA $260,000 = $296,400, which is 4.56% of price. Arithmetic on verified statutory rates. See the ULA table on the Projection page.

rows.metric: Effective total transfer tax at or above the upper threshold, computed
rows.note: Computed on $12,000,000: $727,200 total, which is 6.06% of price. Differs from the City's stated 5.95% because the City quotes the rate components rather than the realised percentage including the $2.25/$500 rounding. Both derivations are shown.

rows.metric: Measure ULA cliff cost of crossing the lower threshold
rows.note: Computed: 4% of $5,400,000 = $216,000, incurred in full on a $1 move across the threshold.

rows.metric: Measure ULA cliff cost of crossing the upper threshold
rows.note: Computed: the step from 4% to 5.5% on $10,900,000 = $163,500.
